title: GS Caltex's 'One-Team' Spirit Shines in Futures Tournament - 조선일보
content: Seniors Assist Juniors, Team Practices Together Ahead of 2026 Championship Defense [Danyang=Sports Chosun Lee Jong-seo reporter] GS Caltex’s 2025–2026 Championship Finals victory, which will go down in V-League history. The "one-team spirit," a powerful driving force, also shone in the Futures matches. GS Caltex is participating in the "2026 Korea Industrial Volleyball Association·Professional Volleyball Futures Champ Tournament Danyang Event," held in Danyang, North Chungcheong Province, from the 7th to the 16th. The tournament features professional teams and industrial teams. Professional teams have formed rosters with players who could not participate in many matches during the regular season. Naturally, starting players who were active during the regular season are either rehabilitating or training at the club’s facility. GS Caltex brought its entire squad to this tournament. While the number of players available for matches is limited due to ongoing recovery or rehabilitation, the team practices together in Danyang and moves to the venue collectively. Last season, GS Caltex wrote a "historic spring volleyball" story. After a fierce battle for rankings until the final stages of the season, they dramatically secured third place and earned a spot in the postseason. With Heungkuk Life recording the same number of points to finish fourth, GS Caltex had to start the postseason from the preliminary finals. They defeated Heungkuk Life and Hyundai Engineering & Construction in succession to advance to the Championship Finals, and they also overcame Korea Expressway Corporation. They achieved an "undefeated championship" by winning all six matches without a single loss. GS Caltex became the first V-League team to win the Championship Finals after participating in the preliminary finals and the first third-place team to achieve an undefeated championship. This was GS Caltex’s fourth Championship Finals title (2007–2008, 2013–2014, 2020–2021, 2025–2026). The driving force behind GS Caltex’s victory was their "one-team" mentality. Centered around the "monster foreign player" Gisele Silva, domestic players performed their roles in every aspect. Even when Silva’s stamina was depleted, the team’s collective effort ensured victory. At this Danyang tournament, GS Caltex truly demonstrated what it means to be a team. On match days, the atmosphere was the opposite of the regular season. Senior players personally moved equipment and carried water bottles. They made efforts to create an environment where younger players participating in the tournament could focus entirely on their matches. Captain Yu Seo-yeon said, "Throughout the season, younger players with fewer years of experience helped us a lot. Now it’s their turn to step up, so we try to carry luggage after sets and help move items when getting off the bus." She added with a smile, "It reminded me of the old days." After matches, the seniors also fulfilled their roles as mentors. Yu Seo-yeon explained, "We don’t interfere much with the matches. Players who were starters last season focus on weight training here. However, we do provide feedback after matches when possible." GS Caltex is sailing smoothly in the "Futures Tournament" as well. They have recorded two wins and one loss in three matches, with the loss ending in a full-set battle. Yu Seo-yeon said, "Thanks to our efforts last season, we are able to train like this with good results. I hope the players participating in this tournament will also show great performances."

title: GS Labs agrees to pay $4.87 million to 18 states - including Nebraska, Iowa - in COVID test settlement - WOWT
content:
LINCOLN, Neb. (WOWT) - Nebraska and Iowa are among 18 states that will get a share of nearly $5 million in a settlement with GS Labs over allegations of overpriced and delayed COVID-19 tests at the height of the pandemic. The lawsuit filed by 18 states said GS Labs overcharged patients whose tests were covered by health insurance. Claims filed against the testing company alleged they had charged patients as much as $380 per test to nearly $1,000 for “multi-panel” tests despite advertising no out-of-pocket costs. In 2021, three clients sent First Alert 6 their medical insurance statements showing COVID-19 testing lab bills of $1,500, $1,600, and $2,000. In a response to First Alert 6 on Wednesday, GS Labs “expressly denies the allegations”: “GS Labs was founded in response to the COVID-19 pandemic and ultimately tested more than 1.4 million Americans, identifying approximately 200,000 positive cases. At its peak, GS Labs handled 20–30% of the rapid testing market in states such as Minnesota and Washington. The settlement expressly denies the allegations against GS Labs, and we agreed to resolve the matter to bring a years-long investigation to a close — not because we believe the claims have merit. We remain proud of our more than 3,000 employees, including many led by U.S. military veterans and many who had been displaced by pandemic shutdowns. They kept testing sites open, supported local jobs and communities, and showed up every day during one of the most chaotic periods in modern public health." The $4.87 million settlement includes $3.6 million in restitution to patients: $1.8 million for cash-paying patients who were overcharged for tests, $1.75 million for patients charged administrative fees, and $33,692 for cash-paying patients who didn’t get their test results within three days. In December 2020, a First Alert 6 investigation found that hundreds of COVID GS Labs test results had been delayed. At the time, GS Labs blamed subcontractors ImmunoGenomics and Quest Labs for the hold up. The rest of the settlement, about $1.25 million, will be dispersed to the states in varying amounts. In a news Wednesday news release, Nebraska Attorney General Mike Hilgers said the state will receive $368,403 from that portion of the settlement, bringing the total headed to Nebraska to nearly $1.5 million. “Companies that take advantage of consumers during a difficult time during a pandemic need to be held accountable. GS Labs significantly overcharged Nebraskans for COVID tests. I’m proud of the work of our office alongside our partnering states to negotiate this settlement for consumers,” Hilgers said in a statement. Iowa AG Brenna Bird confirmed that state will get $654,335. From that total, $430,314 will go to Iowans who were charged administrative fees; $59,589 will go to cash-paying Iowans who were overcharged for tests; and $1,751 will be available for Iowans who didn’t receive their test results within three days. The rest — about $163,000 — is Iowa’s share of the $1.25 million payout to the states. “Not only did GS Labs profit by taking advantage of Iowans, but they did so during a national health crisis when many were facing serious health challenges,” Bird said in the Iowa release. “I’m grateful for the work that secured restitution for affected Iowans, and I will continue to protect Iowa consumers from unfair and deceptive practices.” Hilgers and AGs from Kansas, Minnesota, and Washington negotiated the settlement. Other states attaching to the filing, in addition to Iowa, include Alabama, Arizona, Colorado, Illinois, Indiana, Massachusetts, Missouri, New Jersey, North Dakota, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, and South Dakota. Those who believe they are eligible for a refund can submit requests online through the GS Labs website. The company’s compliance will be monitored by the state coalition participating in the lawsuit. Payments will be processed on a rolling basis, so those who believe they qualify are encouraged to complete their refund requests as soon as possible. GS Labs will then contact them via email with more information about the restitution process. While GS Labs is no longer operational, the company has agreed to adhere to certain advertising and sales policies if it ever resumes testing services. title: Iowa AG: GS Labs to pay $4.87M in multistate COVID-19 testing overcharge settlement - KGAN
content: DES Moines, Iowa — Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird announced Wednesday that GS Labs has agreed to a $4.87 million multistate settlement over allegations that the COVID-19 testing company overcharged patients, imposed unlawful fees and failed to deliver test results within promised timeframes during the pandemic. The settlement resolves claims that GS Labs engaged in deceptive business practices between 2020 and 2022 while providing COVID-19 testing services across multiple states. According to the attorneys general involved in the investigation, GS Labs advertised inflated cash prices that were used to justify higher charges to insured patients, charged nearly 30,000 consumers above market rates for COVID-19 tests and failed to provide results within its advertised three-day window. Investigators alleged some patients waited a week or longer to receive results. The states also alleged that despite advertising no out-of-pocket costs for insured patients, GS Labs charged administrative fees of up to $49 per test to approximately 70,000 consumers. “Not only did GS Labs profit by taking advantage of Iowans, but they did so during a national health crisis when many were facing serious health challenges,” Bird said in a statement. “I’m grateful for the work that secured restitution for affected Iowans, and I will continue to protect Iowa consumers from unfair and deceptive practices.” Under the settlement, GS Labs will pay more than $3.6 million in restitution to affected consumers across the participating states. Iowa consumers are eligible for approximately $491,655 in reimbursement, including about $430,314 for administrative fees, nearly $59,589 for alleged overcharges to cash-paying patients and about $1,752 for delayed test results. Eligible Iowa consumers can seek reimbursement through an online claims process at gslabstesting.com. The attorney general’s office said payments will be issued on a rolling basis, and GS Labs will contact affected consumers by email with additional information about the reimbursement process. In addition to consumer restitution, GS Labs will pay $1.25 million to the coalition of states involved in the settlement, including about $162,681 to Iowa. GS Labs has told the states that it is no longer operating and does not currently provide testing services. Under the agreement, if the company resumes testing operations in the future, it must implement changes to its advertising and sales practices to comply with state consumer protection laws. The settlement includes Iowa and the attorneys general of Alabama, Arizona, Colorado, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, New Jersey, North Dakota, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, South Dakota and Washington.

title: ‘Failed on all counts’: Oregon reaches settlement for overpriced COVID tests - KOIN.com
content: PORTLAND, Ore. (KOIN) – Oregon reached a multistate settlement with GS Labs after the company allegedly overcharged patients for COVID-19 tests and failed to deliver timely test results, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield announced Wednesday. The $4.87 million multistate settlement resolves the allegations against the company, officials said. The multistate coalition investigated GS Labs’ testing practices from 2020 through 2022. This included investigating claims that GS Labs intentionally advertised inflated prices for patients who paid in cash for COVID tests, which sometimes reached as high as $380 per test, or almost $1,000 for multi-panel tests, the Oregon Attorney General’s Office explained. Even though GS Labs provided a “discount” from the cash prices, nearly 30,000 patients paid above market rate for the tests, according to the attorneys general. On top of the markup, hundreds of thousands of patients were guaranteed test results within three days, however, the attorneys general said GS Labs failed to deliver on its promise, and at times, took a week or longer to return the results. The attorneys general also claimed that despite GS Labs advertising that insured patients would have no out-of-pocket costs, the company charged administrative fees as high as $49 per test for an estimated 70,000 patients. “When Oregonians needed COVID tests, they deserved straight answers, accurate prices, honest timelines, and results when they were promised,” said Attorney General Rayfield. “GS Labs failed on all counts. This settlement puts money back in the pockets of people who were taken advantage of during one of the most stressful periods of their lives.” A representative for GS Labs did not immediately return KOIN 6 News’ request for comment. Under the terms of the settlement, GS Labs was ordered to pay more than $3.6 million in restitution to patients, including over $1.8 million for patients who paid in cash that were overcharged for tests and over $1.7 million for patients who were charged with administrative fees. Another $33,000 will go to patients who did not receive their COVID tests within three days. According to the Oregon Attorney General’s Office, Oregonians impacted by GS Labs’ practices, will receive more than $142,000 in restitution. Officials are urging Oregonians who were impacted to verify their eligibility for a settlement payment and to apply online for refunds. Eligible consumers include consumers who paid out-of-pocket, consumers who paid over market rate for tests, consumers who paid for results that were not delivered in the advertised turnaround time and consumers who paid administrative fees to GS Labs. Officials said GS Labs will be contacting consumers over email to share more information about the restitution process. Additionally, GS Labs has shown the plaintiff states that the company no longer offers testing services and is not operational. Under the settlement, if the company decides to resume testing services, GS Labs must make several changes to its advertising and sales practices. This includes disclosing the maximum time it could take for patients to receive test results. GS Labs must also report testing results within the advertised timeline, and if the company cannot meet their deadline, it must notify patients of the delay and offer a full refund. GS Labs must also stop charging over market rates for test results and administrative fees. Alongside Attorney General Rayfield, other attorneys general who helped reach a settlement include those representing Alabama, Arizona, Minnesota, Washington, Ohio and Pennsylvania.

title: Overcharged for a COVID test in Minnesota? You may get money back - KIMT
content: SAINT PAUL, Minn. — Attorney General Keith Ellison announced a $4.87 million multistate settlement with GS Labs that resolves claims the testing company overcharged patients, unlawfully charged administrative fees and failed to deliver timely COVID-19 test results. The multistate coalition, co-led by Ellison, investigated problems with GS Labs' nationwide testing practices from 2020 through 2022. Ellison says the company intentionally advertised inflated cash prices for COVID-19 tests, sometimes as high as $380 per test or nearly $1,000 for multi-panel tests, that were used to justify overcharging patients with insurance coverage. Almost 30,000 patients paid much more than market rate for their COVID-19 tests. For hundreds of thousands of patients, GS Labs allegedly guaranteed test results within three days and failed to deliver on its promise, sometimes taking a week or longer to get test results to patients. Despite advertising that patients with insurance would have no out-of-pocket costs, the company charged administrative fees as high as $49 per test to about 70,000 patients. "I have no patience for pandemic profiteers like GS Labs that deliberately overcharged for COVID-19 tests and deceived Minnesotans about the out-of-pocket costs they would have to pay," Ellison said. "It is also disappointing that GS Labs promised test results in three days that actually took a week or more to deliver." "I'm sure many Minnesotans made plans to travel, to see family, or to attend events that depended on getting quick COVID-19 test results, and GS Labs' failure to produce quick test results caused significant problems in people's lives," Ellison said. "Today's settlement holds GS Labs accountable for overcharging consumers and misrepresenting their services." Under the terms of the settlement filed in Ramsey County District Court, GS Labs will pay more than $3.6 million in restitution to patients. This includes more than $1.8 million for cash-paying patients that were overcharged for tests, more than $1.7 million for patients that were charged administrative fees and $33,692 for cash-paying patients that did not receive test results within three days. Minnesotans that were harmed by GS Labs' testing practices will receive $442,847.50 in restitution through the settlement. The settlement creates an online restitution mechanism that will be funded and run by GS Labs, with oversight by the multistate coalition. Eligible consumers include out-of-pocket paying consumers who paid in excess of the market rate for testing, consumers who paid for test results that were not delivered within the advertised turn-around time and consumers who paid administrative fees to GS Labs. To determine eligibility and receive a restitution payment, consumers must complete a brief verification process at www.gslabstesting.com. The company will also pay $1.25 million to the multistate group, which includes a payment of $146,531.65 to Minnesota. GS Labs has told the states that it no longer offers testing services and is not operational. As part of the settlement, if GS Labs decides to resume testing services, the company must make several changes to its advertising and sales practices. GS Labs must disclose in its marketing materials the maximum time for it to disclose test results. The company will report testing results within the advertised time period and, if it cannot, it must notify patients of the delay and offer a full refund. GS Labs must comply with local, state and federal requirements to promptly deliver COVID-19 test results and provide notification of any delays. GS Labs will stop charging cash-paying patients fees in excess of market rates, charging patients for late test results and charging administrative fees in violation of state and federal laws. The company must disclose in its marketing materials the actual cash price that will be charged to patients, including clearly disclosing any applicable discounts. GS Labs cannot charge administrative fees for COVID-19 testing services or unjustifiably increase the cost of its testing services during a declared emergency. Along with Minnesota, the settlement was negotiated by Kansas, Nebraska and Washington. Joining the settlement are the attorneys general of Alabama, Arizona, Colorado, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Massachusetts, Missouri, New Jersey, North Dakota, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania and South Dakota. title: OPM Proposes Ending Time-in-Grade Rules for GS Promotions - Clearance Jobs
content: The Office of Personnel Management has released a significant new proposal that would eliminate the long‑standing Time‑in‑Grade (TIG) requirement for General Schedule promotions. If finalized, this change would remove the mandatory 52‑week service requirement at each grade level for GS‑5 and above—one of the most notable updates to federal promotion policy in decades. OPM describes the TIG rule as an outdated safeguard from an earlier era of federal personnel management. While originally designed to prevent favoritism and ensure fairness, the agency now argues that today’s structured merit‑based systems already provide the necessary protections. According to OPM, removing TIG would allow agencies to promote employees based on demonstrated readiness rather than time served, helping modernize the federal career ladder. The proposal is currently open for public comment through July 27, and supports the President’s Executive Order to reform the federal hiring process. Under the proposed rule, TIG would no longer be a factor in determining promotion eligibility. Employees would still need to meet all qualification standards and demonstrate the ability to perform at the higher grade, but agencies would gain the flexibility to promote individuals as soon as they are prepared for increased responsibility. If adopted, the rule could reshape the promotion experience across government. Many employees may see earlier opportunities for advancement, especially in career fields where skills develop rapidly. However, the impact may vary by agency. Some organizations may embrace faster promotions, while others may continue to apply conservative internal policies. Importantly, the proposal does not change qualification standards, competitive merit procedures, or the requirement to demonstrate the ability to perform at the higher grade. Agencies must still follow all merit system principles and ensure fair, transparent promotion processes. The proposal is now in the public comment phase. Federal employees, unions, and agencies are encouraged to review the details and submit feedback through the Federal Register. title: UPSC Mains Answer Practice — GS 2 : Questions on India’s CPEC concerns and India-Bhutan relations (Week 158) - The Indian Express
content: UPSC Essentials brings to you its initiative for the practice of Mains answer writing. It covers essential topics of static and dynamic parts of the UPSC Civil Services syllabus covered under various GS papers. This answer-writing practice is designed to help you as a value addition to your UPSC CSE Mains. Attempt today’s answer writing on questions related to topics of GS-2 to check your progress. 🚨 Click Here to read the UPSC Essentials magazine for May 2026. Share your views and suggestions in the comment box or at manas.srivastava@indianexpress.com🚨 Examine the strategic implications of CPEC for India and discuss India’s response to safeguard its interests. India-Bhutan relations are often regarded as the most successful example of India’s ‘Neighbourhood First’ policy. Discuss the factors responsible for this success. QUESTION 1: Examine the strategic implications of CPEC for India and discuss India’s response to safeguard its interests. Relevance: The issue links India’s neighbourhood policy, China-Pakistan relations, sovereignty concerns in PoK, and Indo-Pacific geopolitics. It also highlights connectivity, diplomacy and strategic competition in South Asia. Such themes might appear in GS-2 under International Relations and India’s interests abroad. Note: This is not a model UPSC answer. It only provides you with a thought process which you may incorporate into the answers. — The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), the flagship project of China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), connects China’s Xinjiang region to Pakistan’s Gwadar Port by a network of roads, trains, and pipelines. While promoted as an economic corridor, its strategic ramifications are vital for India’s security and regional interests. — The MEA also criticised “the so-called China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) projects,” claiming that some of them were on Indian sovereign territory and opposing “moves by other countries to reinforce or legitimise Pakistan’s illegal and forcible occupation.” You may incorporate some of the following points in your answer: Focusing on infrastructure development, CPEC was launched in 2015 and connects China’s Xinjiang region with Pakistan’s Gwadar Port on the Arabian Sea. The recent joint statement confirmed plans to further develop the Gwadar Port and Karakoram Highway under the CPEC to expand trade. Another potential aim for China is to bypass the Strait of Malacca, a maritime chokepoint in Southeast Asia, to receive imports from West Asia. It can provide an alternative in case of a blockade or disruption, like the one unfolding in the Strait of Hormuz today. The biggest concern for India is the clear violation of sovereignty due to Pakistan’s illegal occupation of Kashmir, which is rightfully ours. — India has consistently rejected it on the basis of sovereignty. For example, the Karakoram Highway runs through Gilgit-Baltistan in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), a territory claimed by India. — The new offer from China and Pakistan to third parties to participate in CPEC has the potential to attract foreign investment. Such cooperation may strengthen Pakistan’s administrative authority over PoK. — Gwadar Port is seen as part of China’s “String of Pearls” plan, which aims to construct a network of important ports throughout the Indian Ocean. The chain extends from Djibouti in the Horn of Africa to Gwadar in Pakistan, Hambantota and Colombo in Sri Lanka, Chittagong in Bangladesh, Sittwe in Myanmar, and the Ream Naval Base in Cambodia. — India’s most direct response has been supporting the development of the Chabahar port in Iran, which is located just 72 km from Gwadar. It gives India an anchor in the Arabian Sea and also direct access to Afghanistan and Central Asia, bypassing Pakistan completely. — Further north in the Arabian Sea is the port of Duqm in Oman. India secured access to it for military use and logistical support in 2018 and then renewed it in 2021, placing Indian naval assets directly opposite Gwadar. — In Sri Lanka, China sought to maintain a presence through the port of Hambantota, which was built with Chinese loans and leased to a Chinese company for 99 years in 2017. However, in 2025, India and Sri Lanka signed a five-year defence cooperation MoU, reaffirming that Sri Lanka’s territory won’t be used in ways that threaten India’s security interests. (Source: With its latest statement on CPEC, recalling how India has sought to counter China in South Asia) Try this in your answer: Evaluate the effectiveness of India’s responses by examining their achievements and limitations. For instance, while Chabahar Port has enhanced connectivity, sanctions-related constraints persist; access to Duqm Port has expanded India’s maritime reach, but it cannot fully counter Gwadar’s strategic value; and although India’s regional diplomacy has strengthened partnerships, China’s economic influence in the neighbourhood remains substantial. Why does India view CPEC as a challenge to its sovereignty and territorial integrity? How effective have initiatives such as Chabahar Port, IMEC, SAGAR, and the Quad been in protecting India’s interests? ‘The West is fostering India as an alternative to reduce dependence on China’s supply chain and strategically to counter China’s political and economic dominance.’ Explain this statement with examples. (2024) ‘China is using its economic relations and positive trade surplus as tools to develop potential military power status in Asia’. In the light of this statement, discuss its impact on India as her neighbour. (2017) QUESTION 2: India-Bhutan relations are often regarded as the most successful example of India’s ‘Neighbourhood First’ policy. Discuss the factors responsible for this success. Relevance: India-Bhutan relations are often cited as a model of successful neighbourhood diplomacy based on trust, development partnership, and strategic cooperation. The topic covers bilateral relations, regional security, connectivity, and India’s Neighbourhood First policy. It is relevant for GS-2 questions on India’s relations with neighbouring countries. Note: This is not a model UPSC answer. It only provides you with a thought process which you may incorporate into the answers. — India and Bhutan have an extraordinary bilateral relationship based on mutual trust, respect, and common development goals. India-Bhutan relations demonstrate the warmth and confidence that define the two countries’ relationships. This cooperation is widely recognised as the most successful implementation of India’s Neighbourhood First strategy. — The nations’ friendship has grown stronger throughout time, defined by mutual support, understanding, and a common vision of peace, prosperity, and the well-being of our people. You may incorporate some of the following points in your answer: — Unlike many South Asian relationships marred by mistrust and political conflicts, India-Bhutan connections are built on trust and goodwill. Bhutan sees India as its closest and most reliable development partner. — India has played a critical role in Bhutan’s socioeconomic transition by investing in infrastructure, education, healthcare, and capacity building. — Bhutan regards India as a vital partner in implementing this transformative economic initiative. Energy cooperation has resulted in a mutually beneficial relationship, promoting Bhutan’s development and enhancing economic interdependence. — Close society connections, cultural links, and regular exchanges strengthen the relationship, generating goodwill in addition to governmental engagement. — The friendship between Bhutan and India has continued to deepen, adapting to new aspirations while remaining firmly anchored in mutual trust and goodwill. India’s support has extended beyond Bhutan’s immediate development priorities to embrace our long-term national aspirations. — Mangdechhu Hydroelectric Power Project: It is an environmentally friendly run-of-the river scheme, located on river Mangdechhu in Trongsa Dzongkhag in Central Bhutan. The project was inaugurated by Prime Minister of India, Narendra Modi in August 2019. — Kholongchhu Hydroelectric Power Project: It is 600 MW run-of-the-river in the lower course of Kholongchhu river in Trashiyangtse district of Bhutan. It is the first HEP in Bhutan to be implemented under the Joint Venture model, by a JV-company between Druk Green Power Corporation(DGPC) of Bhutan and SJVN Ltd. of India. — Digital Drukyul Flagship Program: India is providing support to components of the program, viz. E-Business National Single Window, Bhutan Integrated Taxation System, Integrated Citizen Services, Digital School, Enhancement of ICT sector’s Capability and Capacity and the Government Initiated Network. (Source: PM of Bhutan writes: PM Modi, my friend, mentor, big brother, congratulations, indembthimphu.gov.in) What role does hydropower cooperation play in strengthening the partnership? content: Three-film series highlights empathy, selflessness and human connection MUMBAI: Not all geniuses solve equations some simply know how to make someone else’s day a little brighter. Parle-G is redefining what it means to be a genius with the latest chapter of its long-running ‘G Maane Genius’ campaign, shifting the spotlight from academic achievement and conventional success to something far simpler and arguably more powerful: kindness. Built around the theme “Genius Wahi Jo Auron Ki Khushi Mein Paye Apni Khushi”, the campaign comprises three films School Drop, Family Tree and Asura, each exploring how empathy, thoughtfulness and selfless actions can leave a lasting impact on others. Rather than celebrating extraordinary accomplishments, the films focus on everyday moments that often go unnoticed. In School Drop, a young boy chooses another person’s needs over his own. Family Tree centres on preserving cherished family bonds and memories, while Asura tells a story rooted in compassion, understanding and emotional connection. Together, the three narratives expand the brand’s interpretation of genius, suggesting that true brilliance may lie not in standing out from others, but in lifting others up. The campaign arrives at a time when success is often measured through milestones, achievements and social recognition. Parle-G’s latest storytelling effort takes a different route, highlighting people whose greatest accomplishment is creating happiness for those around them. Commenting on the campaign, Parle Products vice president Mayank Shah said the brand has long believed that genius extends beyond traditional markers of success. “For decades, Parle-G has celebrated a definition of genius that goes beyond conventional measures of success. With this latest chapter of ‘G Maane Genius’, we wanted to spotlight a quality that is often overlooked today, the ability to create happiness for others,” Shah said. He added that the stories are intended to encourage a broader conversation around what society chooses to recognise and celebrate. For a brand that has been a fixture in Indian households for generations, the campaign leans into emotional storytelling rather than product-led messaging. The focus remains firmly on human values, with the biscuit serving as a familiar backdrop to relatable moments of goodness. In an advertising landscape often dominated by spectacle and scale, Parle-G’s latest effort makes a quieter point, sometimes the most remarkable acts are the simplest ones. And in a world chasing extraordinary success, the campaign argues that helping someone smile may be a form of genius in itself. title: 2026 BMW F 450 GS Review: A True GS - But Should You Buy It? - Car and Bike
content: The GS badge on a BMW has always meant something special. For decades, it has been considered the gold standard of adventure motorcycling. Now, BMW Motorrad brings that legacy to a lighter, more accessible package, in the new BMW F 450 GS. Powered by a light, 420cc, parallel-twin engine, and made-in-India, the F 450 GS replaces the G 310 GS as the entry-level model in the GS family. But does it truly live up to the iconic GS name? And more importantly, should you be reaching for your cheque book? We spent a few days with the top-spec variant of the new F 450 GS to find out what it offers and try and discover its strengths and chinks in its armour. Read on, to know everything about its positives and negatives. Look at the F 450 GS from any angle, and one thing is immediately clear – this is unmistakably a GS. The beak up front, the overall lines, the stance and the way the overall design flows, it's all textbook GS. One glance and know exactly which family it belongs to - underscored by the X-shaped LED headlight down to the slim and narrow rear. The design language draws directly from BMW’s flagship R 1300 GS, right down to the GS Trophy colours on our test bike. What's impressive is how well the proportions work at this size. The F 450 GS looks like a proper GS – tall and commanding – yet but it's surprisingly compact, with a short wheelbase and a kerb weight of just 178 kg. That's lighter than a KTM 390 Adventure, which tells you a lot about what BMW has achieved here. Set out on a ride, and the F 450 GS will immediately impress you with its ergonomics. The riding position is well thought out – upright, neutral, and comfortable for long days in the saddle. Wind protection, however, is one area where the 450 GS leaves you wanting more, particularly if you're considering covering inter-state distances regularly. Taller riders or those planning serious touring will want to factor that in. For my 5’9” frame, the size seems near perfect, and even the 845mm seat height offers decent reach to the ground, on both sides, if that’s a consideration for some. On the flip side though, the size will have taller riders finding it a bit “too compact” and shorter riders – those below 5’7” height – may find the seat height a tad daunting. The new 420cc parallel-twin with a unique 135-degree crankshaft firing order is what underpins the baby GS’ performance. The twin gives it a throaty, mechanical growl rather than the refined hum you'd typically expect from a parallel-twin unit. It's fair to say the sound is an acquired taste rather than something that will immediately impress you. I for one, didn’t quite like it at first, but started warming up to the sound and character of the engine over time. What will impress you, though, is the midrange pull. From just above 3,000rpm all the way to over 7,000 rpm, the engine is eager and rewarding – whether you're overtaking on a highway or getting ahead of city traffic. This is where the torque band of the F 450 GS is, and it offers decent punch and pull in this rev range. And this translates into strong pull without feeling the need to downshift frequently, or to twist the throttle aggressively for the engine to wake up to any needed occasion. The Baby GS can comfortably reach speeds in excess of 150 kmph, but at over 7,000 rpm - in 6th gear, this will be around 120 kmph - is when you will feel some minor buzz in the handlebar and the footpegs. It's not alarming or takes the experience away, but it's there, just so you know.  The GS also misses out on cruise control - for those who like using it (I don't) - but does get heated grips, something which isn't of much use in Indian riding conditions unless you head to the high mountains. And even in peak summer, the engine heat management is surprisingly well sorted for a parallel-twin. When it comes to engine heat, the F 450 GS is perhaps one of those rare motorcycles which doesn’t make you feel it – in traffic, on the highway, and even off-road. The Easy Ride Clutch, or ERC on the F 450 GS is essentially a centrifugal clutch which allows automatic clutch operation without the need for manual input – in this case, the clutch lever. It prevents stalling and offers other benefits. In daily commuting and city traffic, the Easy Ride Clutch is genuinely useful. Paired with the quickshifter, riding the baby GS in urban conditions becomes remarkably easy, almost scooter-like in its effortlessness. You do need to change gears, but once you set off, you can completely ignore the clutch lever. Lever effort on the ERC is on the firm side though, and how the manual clutch actually feels, is a story for another day, when we do get the bike for a test. That said, the ERC does require some adjustment. You need to get the revs up to around 2,700 rpm for it to engage smoothly. It’s something that takes getting used to, particularly off-road. But once you get used to it, and have it in the correct rev range, it’s easy to get used to – quickly. However, there are a few notable downsides to the ERC. It offers no braking assistance on slopes. On inclines or hill climbs, the absence of a hill-hold control or parking brake is a genuine miss. And even with the strong and widely spread torque curve, the system will keep warning you to downshift – just in case you end up lugging the engine. It’s a safety feature, but newer riders may inadvertently tend to lug the engine at higher gears, and that could lead to clutch damage over time. Replacing the ERC will certainly prove to be expensive. The F 450 GS is equally at home on a twisty tarmac road as it is on a dirt trail. With a 19-inch front wheel and predictable, confidence-inspiring road manners, handling is one of its stronger suits. The IMU-powered electronics suite, complete with customisable modes including Enduro Pro, means it punches well above its class on the technology front. Suspension does the job well and won't throw you off balance, but it leans on the firmer side. On our Trophy test bike, the front-end feel is excellent, but the rear remains a touch firm. Compared to the Himalayan 450, which sets a strong benchmark in the mid-size ADV segment, the 450 GS has a noticeably firmer ride. Not stiff, but not as plush either. Riders considering the base variant should note that adjustable suspension isn't on offer there, which makes it harder to assess how absorbent the ride could be with the right setup. Braking performance is pretty good. The single 310 mm front disc brake with a four-piston caliper offers strong and confident stopping power and is more than adequate. Cornering ABS adds another layer of safety to the braking system. Take it off-road and after the first 10 minutes you will soon appreciate that this is a true GS. The taut chassis, the suspension (even with 180mm travel) and the crisp and predictable throttle response all come together to offer you confidence and trust that will make many riders appreciate the package. Enduro Pro mode offers full customisability in throttle response and traction control intervention, while wheelie control and rear wheel ABS are deactivated. Many would argue against alloy wheels and the 19-inch front and 17-inch rear wheel combination. In our experience, in a mix of gravel trails, broken roads and sandy sections, the suspension, handling and stock tyres strike an ideal balance between street performance and off-road protection. The stock Maxxis dual-purpose block pattern tyres didn’t leave us wanting for more performance – on tarmac and off it. And the 220mm of ground clearance is more than adequate for any kind of off-road excursion. In any case, the F 450 GS is an ADV, not a bike meant for enduro or motocross riding. After gunning it down a few dirt trails and over some dusty and sandy off-road patches, the F 450 GS blew me away! It’s surprisingly well-behaved off-road and will make many a newbie adventure rider feel confident about venturing off-tarmac – something which is always a solid character in any ADV motorcycle. This is where potential buyers need to do their homework. BMW service costs come at a premium, and the F 450 GS will be no different. Factor in ownership and running expenses carefully before committing to the showroom price. It's an important part of the ownership equation that goes beyond the sticker price. Yes, there will be service packages offered by BMW Motorrad, but it’s still common knowledge that overall service costs will be more expensive than rivals in its class. Introductory prices for the BMW F 450 GS start at Rs. 4.70 lakh (Ex-showroom), going up to Rs. 5.3 lakh (Ex-showroom) for the top-spec Trophy variant which adds the Easy Ride Clutch and adjustable suspension. The lower variants are available only in black, while the Trophy gets the striking BMW Motorsport colours. It’s worth noting that the Sport variant, which comes with a manual clutch, adjustable suspension, and a red colour option, is not currently on sale in India, yet. There’s no confirmed timeline on that either, so waiting for it isn’t a decision we’d recommend making right now. There’s also the broader question of value. Rivals like the Royal Enfield Himalayan 450 and the KTM 390 Adventure R are available at significantly lower prices. Yes, they are single-cylinder machines, and they don’t carry the GS badge. But the price difference is substantial enough to fully kit yourself out in quality riding gear and still have change to spare for a couple of long adventure rides. Whether that trade-off makes sense is a conversation only you can have with yourself. The BMW F 450 GS is a genuinely impressive motorcycle. Great design, a solid feature set, and it absolutely earns the GS badge. Excellent road manners, capable off-road performance, and a package that even newbie ADV riders will find approachable, the F 450 GS offers a lot that’s hard to ignore. If you're considering one, go ride it. But our advice is to test it without the Easy Ride Clutch first. Ride it like a regular motorcycle, because that's how you'll truly know if it's the right fit for you. You need to be comfortable with the mechanical sound, the engine's character, and the seat height. And if you're opting for the manual variant in India, keep in mind that adjustable suspension won't be part of the package. Overall, it's a strong, well-rounded motorcycle. And unlike its predecessor, the G 310 GS, this one is a true GS through and through. Just make sure the running costs fit your budget before you sign on the dotted line.

title: Retired Bombay HC Judge Justice GS Patel and Family Face Sustained Threats Over Dawoodi Bohra Verdict - LawStreet Journal
content: Mumbai: Retired Bombay High Court judge Justice G.S. Patel and his family have allegedly been subjected to a sustained campaign of threats and violence in India and the United Kingdom, reportedly linked to his April 2024 judgment in the decade-long Dawoodi Bohra community leadership dispute. According to reports, Justice Patel’s daughter was accosted and attacked in London by an unidentified masked individual on April 22 this year, sustaining a fractured nose and being left bloodied. UK counter-terrorism authorities are examining the incident. Over the past ten months, Justice Patel’s family has received multiple threatening communications. The first reported threat occurred in August 2025, when letters were sent to both his Mumbai residence and to his daughter in London. One of the letters claimed responsibility for a break-in at his daughter’s home. The most recent incident was reported on June 5, 2026, when an anonymous letter was sent to his daughter in London, warning of escalating violence and claiming that a contract had been issued against the family. The letter bore a German postal mark and was sent from a fictitious London address. It included a digital storage device, which is now in the custody of Hertfordshire Police. The family chose not to access the device due to security concerns. The communications allegedly demanded that Justice Patel publicly retract his judgment through a YouTube video. The letters also outlined instructions for disseminating such a statement to legal bodies and the media. A non-cognisable complaint had earlier been registered in Mumbai. Law enforcement authorities in the United Kingdom are actively investigating the matter. Justice Patel has reportedly informed the Chief Justice of India, the Acting Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court, and the Indian High Commission in London about the threats and incidents. On April 23, 2024, Justice Patel held that Mufaddal Saifuddin, the 53rd Dai and incumbent leader of the Dawoodi Bohra community, is the rightful leader of the community. He dismissed a suit filed by Taher Fakhruddin, who had challenged Saifuddin’s leadership, on the ground that Fakhruddin could not prove his appointment as the Syedna, the community leader. The verdict is presently under challenge before a Division Bench of the Bombay High Court. The deeply contested succession dispute within the Dawoodi Bohra community arose following the demise of the 52nd Syedna, Mohammad Burhanuddin. His son, Mufaddal Saifuddin, assumed leadership as the 53rd Syedna. This was disputed by Khuzaima Qutbuddin, the half-brother of the deceased leader, who claimed that a secret nass, or conferment of succession, had been made in his favour by the late 52nd leader, making him the rightful Dai al-Mutlaq. When the dispute could not be resolved, Qutbuddin filed a suit before the Bombay High Court on March 29, 2014, seeking a declaration that he was the rightful 53rd Dai. In 2016, while evidence was still being recorded, the original plaintiff passed away and his son, Taher Fakhruddin, was substituted as the plaintiff. The trial ran for nine years before the suit was eventually dismissed in April 2024. title: Preventing Certificate Expiration Incidents… WeBareSoft 'CertBear' Achieves GS Certification Grade 1 - 벤처스퀘어
content: WeBareSoft, a company specializing in API management and security, is accelerating its expansion into the public and financial markets after receiving official recognition for the quality competitiveness of its SSL/TLS certificate automation management solution, 'CertBear'. WeBareSoft announced that its SSL/TLS certificate automation management solution, 'CertBear', has obtained Grade 1 of the GS (Good Software) certification, a nationally recognized software quality certification. GS certification is granted by nationally accredited testing laboratories, such as the Korea Testing & Research Institute (KTR), based on a comprehensive evaluation of functional suitability, performance efficiency, usability, reliability, and security according to international standards ISO/IEC 25023, 25041, and 25051. Grade 1 signifies the highest level of quality and serves as a key requirement for entering the public procurement market and being designated as a priority purchase target by public institutions. With the acquisition of this certification, WeBareSoft has verified the reliability of its products while laying the foundation for expanding its customer base in the public and financial sectors. CertBear is an SSL/TLS certificate lifecycle management platform that utilizes server-specific agent-based port scanning technology to automatically detect certificates and manage public and private certificates in an integrated manner. It is designed to reduce repetitive tasks by automating the entire process from issuance to renewal and distribution, and to enable immediate response to certificate expiration or errors through real-time monitoring and multi-channel notification features. With recent changes in global security policies expected to shorten the validity period of SSL/TLS certificates to a maximum of 47 days by 2029, the burden of certificate management on companies is increasing. WeBareSoft believes that this change will serve as a catalyst for the expansion of the certificate automation market. Based on this GS certification, the company plans to expand adoption, focusing on public institutions and the financial sector, and actively target the demand for preventing certificate expiration accidents and improving operational efficiency. Jang Young-hui, CEO of WeBareSoft, stated, “The GS certification Grade 1 is a result of CertBear being recognized for its ability to operate stably even in large-scale infrastructure environments,” adding, “We will strengthen our targeting of the public and financial markets with a platform capable of responding to the global trend of shortened certificate validity periods.” He further added, “Based on our domestic references, we plan to expand our presence in overseas markets, including Singapore and Southeast Asia.” We Bare Soft has secured a track record of supplying products to the public sector through the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy's Automotive Innovation Industry Open Platform project and registration as an innovative procurement product on the Public Procurement Service's Venture Nara. title: BMW F 450 GS Bookings Temporarily Halted - BikeWale
content: The BMW F 450 GS seems to be witnessing pretty high demand in India. Bookings for the motorcycle across the country have been temporarily halted, even before the commencement of deliveries. The first few batches that were allotted to India have already been booked, and the next booking window is expected to open around September-October 2026. Even before the bookings were paused, the waiting period for the motorcycle was staggeringly long. In fact, dealers in Mumbai and Bengaluru were reporting a waiting period of close to a year. Showrooms in other cities like Kolkata and Hyderabad had a waiting period of somewhere between six and eight months. Looking at where things stand now, anyone interested in buying the F450GS today might have to wait to get the motorcycle for close to year. Even after the next booking window opens later this year, the waiting period from then onwards will be around 6-8 months in almost every city. Customers who had booked the bike between November and December last year are expected to get their motorcycles from next month onwards. This could either be an indication of high demand or slow production of the bike by TVS at its Hosur facility. We have been noticing a similar situation with the TVS Apache RTX, another bike being produced at the same Hosur plant, which also has a long waiting period. Now, whether this is due to some hiccups at the production end or exports of the 450 to the international markets are taking first priority is still not known.

title: GS Caltex GM Kim Yong-hee Leads Volleyball Title with 'Respect Leadership' - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
Kim Yong-hee, GM of Women's Pro Volleyball Champions GS Caltex
From Rank-and-File Staff to GM... More Than 10 Work Logs Filled with Notes
Valuable as Team Archives, "I Try to Honor Everything I Write Down"
United with Coach in Scouting New Faces: "We'll Give Fans New Energy" "What I always keep in mind when dealing with players is respect and consistency. I make sure to treat each player with equal respect and to show no difference in my attitude." GS Caltex won the championship of the 2025-2026 women's professional volleyball season. The team swept Korea Expressway Corporation 3-0 in the championship series to lift the trophy for the first time in five years. Advancing to the postseason as the third seed in the regular league, the team set a first-ever record by winning all six postseason matches. It was a stunning turnaround from the 2024-2025 season, when the team finished sixth out of seven teams. At the center of the turnaround was Kim Yong-hee, the general manager of GS Caltex. It was the first championship he achieved in the three years since taking on the GM role. Meeting with Seoul Economic Daily on Wednesday, Kim was asked about the driving force behind the title and said, "Respect and consideration for all players brought the team's strength together and led to the championship." Kim's "respect leadership" succeeded not simply because of his attitude but thanks to his habit of helping players by noting down even the smallest details. In fact, the diaries he has kept since 2004, when he began working with the volleyball team, number more than 10 volumes. They are densely filled with the team's schedules large and small, notable matters of each moment, unexpected situations such as injuries and the processes of resolving them, and the personal histories of individual players. "Since I've worked across various areas over the years, my memory inevitably has limits, so I took a lot of notes," Kim said. "I wrote down things that could help players or staff and handled them, which allowed things to proceed quickly." He stressed, "I tried to honor everything I wrote down by any means, and I will continue to do so." Kim's diaries are currently stored in the archive room of the team's gymnasium. For the past several years, he has been using a memo application instead of a diary. The journey to the championship also had severe ups and downs. GS Caltex fell into a 14-game losing streak in the 2024-2025 season due to a series of player injuries. Kim arranged a psychological education program for the team and made changes to the atmosphere at the training ground. He sent a coffee truck and printed encouragement messages to post in the locker room. "The losing streak at that time was because injured players appeared all at once, so I made efforts such as looking into overseas treatment for quick recovery," Kim said, looking back. title: A Used Lexus GS-F Could Be The Bulletproof V8 Sedan You've Been Waiting For - CarBuzz
content: Justin Pritchard is a seasoned Sudbury, Ontario-based automotive journalist, producer, and technical writer. With a passion for cars and a talent for storytelling, he's established himself as a prominent figure in the Canadian automotive scene. His work, which encompasses automotive reviews, insightful analyses, and stunning photography, is featured across multiple Canadian television programs, print publications, and online platforms. Justin's dedication to his craft has earned him numerous awards and accolades, solidifying his reputation as a trusted voice in the automotive industry. The Lexus GS F is a now-discontinued naturally aspirated V8 performance sedan that gives second-hand shoppers a cheaper, less complex alternative to high-performance four-doors such as the BMW M5 and Mercedes-Benz E63 of the era. With more powerful turbocharged competitors commanding premium prices, the GS F is a particularly enticing deal for the driving enthusiast after something extremely rare and well known for bulletproof dependability. Could a used Lexus GS F be the hidden gem opportunity you’ve been looking for? Below, let's get up to speed on this often-overlooked application of one of the market’s most storied V8 engines. It's a free-breathing 5.0-liter tuned by Yamaha like a musical instrument. 5.0-liter V8, 90-degree with aluminum block and cylinder heads In the 2010s, a battle for V8 supremacy, decades in the making, was coming to a head. The sports and performance car scene was now being powered by some of the most powerful and daring engines it had ever seen. The Cadillac CTS-V was making 640 horsepower from a supercharged V8. The Mustang Shelby GT350 was producing 526 hp from an 8,250-RPM V8 with a flat-plane crank. FCA dropped the Hellcats into the mix during this era as well, a little late to the party but packing over 700 supercharged horsepower. If you wanted exotic-car horsepower output without the exotic-car price tag, this was a good time to be shopping for V8 power. For context, the market at the time was also shifting away from naturally aspirated V8 engines (as well as sedans in general) in much of the luxury and performance space. Turbocharged four- and six-cylinder alternatives were more easily tuned to comply with tightening economy and emissions targets. To meet ever-higher demands for horsepower, many of the remaining V8 engines were supercharged or turbocharged, enabling them to surpass the output figures of some V10 and V12 engines from years earlier. The horsepower party was pumping, and Lexus was busy doubling down on its 2UR-GSE V8 engine. The 5.0-liter quad-cam unit was a gem of an engine, originally launched with 416 horsepower in the 2007 Lexus IS-F. Tuned by Yamaha like a musical instrument, it’s one of the most fascinating V8 engines of the modern era, thriving with natural aspiration as competitors received forced induction. Over the years, Lexus gently improved the V8 with a mid-cycle update, and quickly quadrupled the number of vehicles it would power. The RC F Coupe arrived for the 2015 model year with 467 hp, bringing the 5.0-liter engine's improved output to a new performance coupe chassis with a trick torque-vectoring rear axle. The following year, for 2016, the GS F joined the mix as well, powering Lexus’s rear-drive luxury sport sedan with the 5.0-liter V8 for the first time. Two years later, the LC 500 arrived as an additional (but pricey) way to experience the 2UR-GSE. When Lexus launched the GS F, their V8-powered performers had plenty of momentum. The IS F sedan was well established, and the RC-F had given shoppers a more athletic, two-door alternative. When the GS F arrived, a few factors were working against it getting more traction than it probably deserved. This rear-drive-only model was playing in a field increasingly populated by AWD alternatives. The GS’s platform and infotainment were also four years old by the time the GS F arrived, a lifetime in the luxury scene. You could just as easily buy something from BMW, Mercedes, Cadillac, or Audi on a more modern platform with more modern tech. Numerous competitors offered Android Auto and Apple CarPlay, not available at the GS F’s launch – though it did have a CD player. The GS F wasn't the fastest take on the 5.0-liter V8, but arguably, it was the most comfortable. Think 'hot-rod cruiser' more than an all-out track weapon, and you're in the right ballpark. In Normal or Eco mode, the GS F was hardly any more engaging or stimulating to your senses than a Toyota Corolla. Flicked into Sport or Sport Plus mode, the sensation of the GS-F flexing, breathing harder, and tensing up for action all around the driver was hard to forget. For a rear-drive machine, it launched quickly and with minimal drama on bare pavement. There was just the right amount of wheelspin before the velvety V8 power curve started to stuff your seatback into your backside. Still, the GS F was a bigger, slower application of the 5.0-liter V8 than the IS-F sports sedan or striking RC-F Coupe, meaning it wasn't the F car to buy if you were after the ultimate thing. Many shoppers were after the maximum bang for their performance dollar, where the GS F was closer to the bottom of the charts in that respect. For similar money, your buddy's Dodge Charger Hellcat would eat your GS-F for lunch. Still, the GS F blended the tidy dynamics of the GS with the all-motor V8 experience of the 2UR-GSE, but shoppers after maximum excitement for their money had better alternatives. Though it likely wasn’t a dealbreaker for many, the GS F also used a speaker-enhanced sound system to amplify the engine and exhaust sounds by playing supplemental sounds over the stereo system. Partially, this was because the GS platform was engineered to be so quiet that drivers might otherwise have trouble hearing the V8 at a satisfying volume at full song. Many enthusiast drivers prefer a pure approach to the soundtrack, and may have chosen something else instead. This is not only the most affordable V8-powered performance sedan on the market today, but it may also be the only affordable V8 sports sedan left. The total number of units produced is a bit tricky to nail down, since Lexus only reported total sales for the GS model range and never specifically identified the GS-F as a separate entity in its sales reporting. On ClubLexus.com, a forum member posted the response they received from Lexus after asking about final production numbers. The results are summarized below. From its original starting price of around $85,000, you’ll likely be paying somewhere around half that amount for a second-hand GS F today, though there are always exceptions. According to online data, you can expect to pay between $40,000 and $50,000 for a second-hand GS-F these days, with some extremely pristine, low-mileage examples pushing to $70,000 or more. Shop patiently, though. The low production volumes mean used units don't come up very often. Still, rising interest may pull more and more units out of storage and into the used-car market. A combination of the 5.0-liter V8’s reputation for bulletproof reliability and the GS F’s rarity in the marketplace are contributing to increasing interest. The same goes for its ‘last-of-its-kind’ engine. Notably, this high-performing V8 is free of the complex turbocharging systems common in competitor models. It isn’t widely known for any major or systematic issues, unlike, say, the cylinder head bolts in the Mercedes M156 V8 engine of the same era. According to RepairPal, maintenance costs average just $499 per year. For a high-performance luxury sedan, that’s a steal of a deal when ongoing maintenance and repair costs are considered. Be sure to note the $4,300 annual fuel cost as well, with premium unleaded required. How Two Japanese Titans Built One Of The World's Best V8s Note that many owners enjoy driving these cars as often as possible, and a few treat them as collector items. Today, you’ll probably pay $57,000 for a used GS-F with under 50,000 miles on its odometer on the high side, and around $47,000 for a unit with closer to 100,000 miles of former use. The same $47,000 could also get you into a nearly new Infiniti Q50 Red Sport 400 that’s five years newer with less than 40,000 miles. For the same money as a low-mileage GS-F, you’re also handily into a nearly-new BMW M440i, likely with a sub-20,000-mile odometer reading. In this way, you can see the premium some shoppers are willing to pay for the GS F's rarity, unique engine, and likelihood of excellent reliability for the long haul. With smart shoppers increasingly choosing proven, old-school, naturally aspirated engines as a financial power move for the future, it’s probably a great time for shoppers to get serious about pulling the trigger on a used GS F, if they’re able to find one. title: GS Neotek Unveils AI-Based Method to Cut Incident Analysis Time at AWS Summit - Seoul Economic Daily
content: GS Neotek announced Tuesday that it presented an artificial intelligence (AI)-based methodology for shortening incident analysis at the "Amazon Web Services (AWS) Ambassador Global Summit 2026," held in Seattle on June 3. This year's event drew a total of 129 AWS Ambassadors from 29 countries, who shared technology strategies, service directions, and customer success stories. AWS Ambassador is a designation granted to experts within the AWS Partner Network (APN) who have demonstrated their ability to strengthen AWS capabilities within their organizations and exhibit external technical leadership. At the summit, Choi Sung-woo, an AI research engineer at GS Neotek's AI Center, gave a presentation titled "Petabyte-Scale Root Cause Analysis Completed in 20 Minutes." Choi introduced a methodology that reduces the context delivered to large language models (LLMs) by about 80 percent through a generative AI-based "incident agent" architecture. This applies to the root cause analysis (RCA) process, which previously took up to three hours and 30 minutes in environments with petabyte-scale operational data and peak traffic. Using this method, tool calls can be parallelized to cut response time by about four times compared with sequential processing. Choi also introduced practical operational patterns that help internal and external operators perform rapid and repetitive incident analysis using only natural language commands. Choi received a special award at the event, the "AWS Ambassador Certification All-Star Award." The award honors the achievements of ambassadors who have contributed to customer success and technical leadership within the AWS ecosystem, recognizing their expertise and capability development across various technical domains including AWS architecture, development, operations, security, and data. title: Goldman Sachs (GS) Has a Fee, Financing, and Wealth Engine Bigger Than the Deal Cycle - AlphaStreet
content: Goldman Sachs is still often framed as a stock that simply needs mergers and capital markets to reopen. The firm’s latest filings suggest that description is too narrow. Deal activity still matters, but Goldman’s current earnings mix looks broader: investment banking has improved, equities financing remains strong, and Asset & Wealth Management is contributing more fee-based stability than the old cycle-only narrative implies. The headline quarter was strong enough to support that view. Goldman reported first-quarter 2026 net revenues of $17.23 billion and net earnings of $5.63 billion, with diluted EPS of $17.55 and annualized return on average common shareholders’ equity of 19.8%. Those are not the numbers of a franchise waiting passively for one market window to reopen. They reflect multiple revenue engines working at once. Investment banking was the most obvious swing factor, and it was clearly better. Goldman said investment banking fees were $2.84 billion in the first quarter, up 48% from the prior year, driven by significantly higher advisory revenue and stronger equity underwriting, with debt underwriting also higher despite weaker leveraged finance activity. That matters, but the release also said the firm’s investment banking fees backlog only decreased slightly from year-end 2025. In other words, the rebound is real, but Goldman is not presenting itself as a one-quarter M&A trade. The bigger point is what sat alongside banking. Net revenues in Global Banking & Markets reached $12.74 billion, up 19% from the prior year. Within that, Equities was especially important because Goldman said higher financing revenues, particularly prime financing, helped offset weaker areas elsewhere. Fixed Income, Currency and Commodities generated $4.01 billion, down 10% year over year, but that weakness did not derail the quarter because the franchise was carried by mix rather than by one perfect macro backdrop. For investors, that is a more useful signal than simply noting whether IPOs or M&A volumes improved. Asset & Wealth Management adds another layer to the thesis. Net revenues there were $4.08 billion, up 10% from the prior year. Goldman attributed the improvement primarily to higher management and other fees, reflecting higher average assets under supervision, while the 10-Q also said incentive fees were higher and investments were stronger. That is exactly the sort of revenue that changes how the firm should be valued. Asset- and advice-linked fees are not immune to markets, but they are structurally different from episodic underwriting revenue. They make Goldman look more like a platform that can monetize client assets, lending, advisory, and private-market exposure across cycles. The 10-Q also helps explain why financing deserves more attention in the Goldman story. The firm said market making revenues reflected significantly higher financing activity, especially in equities financing, even as intermediation revenue in some fixed-income businesses softened. That reinforces the idea that Goldman’s client franchise is valuable not just when boards announce deals, but when hedge funds, institutions, and wealth clients keep using the balance sheet and market infrastructure. Platform Solutions remains the obvious counterpoint, but even that weakness supports the broader thesis. Net revenues there were $411 million, down from $610 million a year earlier, and Goldman said the decline primarily reflected net markdowns tied to the Apple Card loan portfolio, which had already been transferred to held for sale in 2025. That segment still creates noise, yet it is increasingly less central to the franchise than the market once feared. Goldman is effectively narrowing back toward the businesses where it has stronger economics and better competitive advantages. Capital return adds another clue about management’s confidence in the mix. During the quarter, Goldman returned $6.38 billion to common shareholders, including $5.00 billion of repurchases and $1.38 billion of common stock dividends, while book value per share rose 1.0% to $361.19 and the Common Equity Tier 1 ratio stood at 12.5% under the standardized rules. A firm that can post near-20% ROE while returning that much capital is demonstrating earnings breadth, not just cyclical torque. Goldman will always be partly judged on whether dealmaking stays healthy. But the primary filings now show a firm with at least three meaningful supports beneath that debate: fee revenue from wealth and asset management, financing-led strength inside the markets franchise, and a capital position that allows heavy shareholder returns. That mix makes Goldman look bigger than a pure advisory-cycle stock.

title: GS E&C Partners With Daedong Robotics to Develop AI Field Robots - Let's Data Science
content: Korean construction firm GS E&C and robotics maker Daedong Robotics signed a memorandum of understanding on June 5 to jointly develop and field-test AI-powered autonomous robots at construction sites, according to the Korea Herald and ChosunBiz. The agreement covers on-site demonstrations of Daedong's autonomous driving robots and joint development of models tailored to construction environments, with an initial focus on material transport and other repetitive tasks, per ChosunBiz and Asiae. The companies say they will run staged on-site tests to verify performance and safety and use trial data to refine operating requirements. Asiae and Seoul Economic Daily note Daedong is expanding its platform from agricultural delivery into manufacturing and construction. The deal is a preliminary MOU, with no budget, timeline or specific robot models disclosed. GS E&C and Daedong Robotics signed a memorandum of understanding on June 5 for collaborative research, development and field demonstrations of AI-powered autonomous field robots at construction sites, according to the Korea Herald and ChosunBiz. The MOU covers on-site demonstrations of Daedong's autonomous driving robots and joint development of robot models suited to the irregular, non-standardized conditions of construction sites, per Asiae and Seoul Economic Daily. Multiple outlets report the initial focus is on material transport and other repetitive tasks that can be automated relatively quickly. Reporting describes Daedong Robotics as an autonomous-robot platform developer that launched publicly in 2024 and is expanding from agricultural delivery into manufacturing and construction. The partners say the collaboration will include staged on-site tests to verify performance and safety and will collect operational data to refine robot functions. Asiae quotes Daedong Robotics CEO Kang Sung-chul on combining the company's AI capabilities with GS E&C's site experience for technology verification. As a general pattern, construction-focused robotics pilots start with material handling and repetitive logistics because those tasks reduce human exposure to hazards and are easier to isolate technically than complex manipulation or finishing work. Platforms moving from agriculture or logistics into construction typically face higher durability, perception and navigation requirements because sites change frequently and mix human and machine traffic. During the pilot phase, useful indicators include how the partners validate safety controls in mixed-traffic zones, what sensing and mapping upgrades dynamic site geometry requires, and whether the trials produce structured datasets that support robustness to construction-specific conditions. Reporting notes the partners intend to use trial data to refine operating requirements, making dataset and safety-procedure design an early deliverable. The sources do not provide timelines, budget figures, the specific robot models to be used, or required regulatory approvals. Coverage centers on the MOU and stated objectives; neither company has published a technical roadmap in the cited articles. A non-binding MOU between a major contractor and a commercial robotics maker is a credible vertical pilot for construction automation and is relevant to teams building deployable field robots.
